name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,459

clue.text: Dormant man on board wants aid to peaceful retirement

blocks.note: a piece in the board game draughts (checkers)

explanation.surface: A sleeping piece on a game board somehow needs help to rest peacefully.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here is going to bed, not leaving work; draughts is the British name for checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink of medicine taken at bedtime helps someone drift off to sleep, so it assists a calm night.

clue.text: Element in languages discerned by cardinal

indicators.note: to discern is to perceive, here taken as picking up by ear

blocks.note: tongues are languages; the spelling follows the sound

explanation.surface: A chemist spots some element mentioned in languages a cardinal of the church can read.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal is a number, not a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten is a chemical element, the metal with symbol W used in lamp filaments.

clue.text: Stoop that's pronounced in Hamlet?

indicators.note: says we want a word as it is spoken rather than how it is written

blocks.note: to stoop to doing something is to deign

explanation.surface: Someone notes a word for stooping that gets spoken in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark, so the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is a prince of Denmark, so he is one example of a native of that country.

clue.text: Country agents to seize wandering Bloom

indicators.note: letters that wander stray from their places and end up rearranged
seizing means grabbing hold and surrounding something within

explanation.surface: Spies in some country are sent to arrest a man called Bloom who has strayed.
explanation.walkthrough: Leopold Bloom of Ulysses famously wanders Dublin, which flavours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Colombia is a nation in north-western South America, whose capital is Bogotá.

clue.text: Lecture-hall chimney lined by unknown engineer

indicators.note: a lining sits inside, so the second part goes within the first

blocks.note: Scottish and northern word for a chimney
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z

explanation.surface: An anonymous engineer fits the lining inside the lecture hall's chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: Lum is a Scots word for a chimney, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyceum was originally Aristotle's school, and the word came to mean a hall for public lectures.

clue.text: Doctor consulted surgeon about individual

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

explanation.surface: A doctor called in a surgeon to look at one particular patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawbones is old slang for a surgeon or physician, from the days of amputations.

clue.text: Capital retrospective series in November Gazette

indicators.note: a run of consecutive letters sits within the following words
looking back means reading the letters from end to start

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs a series looking back at a capital city in its November edition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain example: this Balkan city is the seat of government of Croatia, so it is one national capital.

clue.text: Where old nations reassembled to act without reserve

indicators.note: putting something together again in a fresh way rearranges its parts

explanation.surface: A query about the place where former countries regrouped to get on with things.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to relax and behave freely, dropping inhibitions, as at a party.

clue.text: Praising Our Lady at Barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go crazy

explanation.surface: A hymn praising the Virgin Mary in Barking, the London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking looks like the east London place name; it is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudatory describes words that extol or commend, the adjective from laud.

clue.text: Not the time before Christ in traditional saying

blocks.note: negated by Not: the era that is not BC, Anno Domini

explanation.surface: A proverb seems to deny something about the era before Christ.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a riddle: a time that is not before Christ is an AD age. Not belongs with before Christ even though the time sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is an old proverb, a piece of wisdom handed down over generations.

clue.text: Artist Coleridge upset after losing identity

indicators.note: losing something means letters drop out of the word
upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the usual short form, as in ID card

explanation.surface: The poet Coleridge suffers an identity crisis and is distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was the Cretan-born painter who worked in Toledo, Spain.

clue.text: Stop doctor boarding E-boat

indicators.note: boarding a vessel means getting inside it

blocks.note: the ship of Jason and the Argonauts

explanation.surface: A medic climbs aboard a German torpedo boat to halt it.
explanation.walkthrough: E-boat looks like one word, the wartime German craft, but splits into E and boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban or halt on trade, so it is a stop.

clue.text: Letter from Eliot answered

indicators.note: taken from within the following words, so the letters lie inside them

blocks.note: the run straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A letter written by Eliot that got a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Still one creates another name for such a snowman

blocks.note: surface reading: a motionless figure gives rise to a fresh name
setter's reading: still is YET and one is I, together the other name for this beast, the yeti

explanation.surface: A frozen figure turns out to be known by some other title.
explanation.walkthrough: YET plus I spells YETI, another name for the creature, so the answer is the word that goes with snowman.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is also called the abominable snowman, the legendary ape-like creature of the Himalayas.

clue.text: Transport moved along accepting fare

indicators.note: things that have been moved are shifted into new positions
accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: as in how did you fare, how did you do

explanation.surface: A vehicle travels on, taking passengers who pay a fare.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is a Venetian boat, or a cable car cabin, either one a means of travel.

clue.text: Measure of resistance encountered in amending Homer

indicators.note: amending means altering, so the letters are changed round
one piece sits inside the other

explanation.surface: Resistance was met when someone tried to edit Homer's epic.
explanation.walkthrough: Resistance looks literary but is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: An ohmmeter is an instrument that gauges electrical resistance in ohms.

clue.text: Tees backing interference over article he saves

indicators.note: backing means standing behind, so this piece follows the next one

blocks.note: meddling, making a mess of things

explanation.surface: The setter supports some meddling over an article about a rescuer.
explanation.walkthrough: Tees is the setter's pseudonym, so he is I, placed behind the interference. The final H appears to come from the start of he, which also serves the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Messiah is the promised deliverer or saviour, the one who brings salvation.

clue.text: Endlessly go without nice surprise? That's abuse!

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: to miss something is to go without it

explanation.surface: Someone who's always denied a nice surprise feels hard done by and protests.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistreat is to handle someone cruelly or badly, which is what abuse means as a verb.

clue.text: Green wall up protecting revolutionary army

indicators.note: revolution turns something round, so the letters run backwards
protecting means enclosing for safety, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: A green wall is put up around a band of rebel soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Wall up looks like two words of instruction but is one verb, IMMURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or unripe, so it matches not yet fully developed.

clue.text: Payment about to arrive with enclosures inside

indicators.note: places this piece within the other

explanation.surface: A cheque about to arrive in the post with some enclosures in the envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Recompense is compensation or reward given for loss or effort, money handed over.

clue.text: Card game gamblers found here

blocks.note: first meaning: a game of cards, also spelt cassino
second meaning: a building for betting

explanation.surface: A game of cards is where you'll find people placing bets.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an old card game for capturing cards and the establishment where people bet money.

clue.text: Reveal river's swelling another?

indicators.note: something swelling grows round what it holds, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: another river, the Exe of Devon
the Italian river Po, with its 's

explanation.surface: Showing how one river's flooding bulges into another.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England; Po and Exe are crossword staples.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose is to uncover or lay bare, a synonym for reveal as a verb.

clue.text: Member returned flanked by two warriors?

definitions.note: an impi is a body of warriors, so the plural is fair

indicators.note: flanked means having something on each side, so one piece is surrounded

blocks.note: Roman numeral for two, split to each side
a Member of Parliament is returned at an election

explanation.surface: An elected representative comes back with a soldier on either side.
explanation.walkthrough: Returned looks like a reversal signal but describes the MP being elected.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a Zulu regiment, an armed band of fighters.

clue.text: Posh little piano with note added shows rising curve

blocks.note: a postscript is a note added to a letter

explanation.surface: A smart small piano with a musical note tacked on displays a rising curve.
explanation.walkthrough: Note added sounds musical but is a postscript; it lands after U.
explanation.definitionFit: An upsweep is an upward curve or sweep, as of hair or a line.

clue.text: Cooked in oven with wine marinade?

indicators.note: marinating soaks something in liquid, so one piece is immersed in the other

explanation.surface: Meat cooked in the oven after soaking in a wine marinade.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, seen as oast houses in Kent; here it sits soaking in red.
explanation.definitionFit: Roasted is the past participle of roast, meaning cooked by dry heat.

clue.text: President after James B murdered second son!

blocks.note: the familiar first name of Lincoln
the initial of the man who succeeded James Buchanan

explanation.surface: A US president follows James Buchanan, then a second son is killed.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln followed Buchanan in the White House: Abe gives ABE and L stands for Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Abel was Adam and Eve's second son, killed by his brother Cain.

clue.text: For this reason chicken vacated cage

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outside letters remain

blocks.note: the word with its insides removed

explanation.surface: That is why the chicken escaped from its cage.
explanation.definitionFit: Hence is a formal adverb meaning therefore, as a consequence.

clue.text: Singular boast about keeping pest controller

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pieces wrap the next

explanation.surface: An odd boast about keeping a pest controller.
explanation.walkthrough: Keeping looks like part of the boast but is its own piece, a synonym for care; about wraps the other two round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarecrow is a figure placed in fields to frighten birds off crops, so it controls pests.
